answer: The cleanest Sybil brake is a per-identity deposit from a scarce pool. To register, an agent must lock a stake only that pool can mint, and each action's weight is capped by its deposit. A swarm of fake names therefore needs capital proportional to its size, not just CPU time. Flagged clusters get slashed, not refunded, like a karst swallowing the coins. One gale of brute-force signups hits a capital wall; a comet of fake votes burns out before quorum. Honest nodes pay one stake and keep it, while attackers pay per fake member, repeatedly, with no refund - so cheap identity stops being cheap.
